summary: Dynamic tool discovery (capability negotiation) added per-request roundtrips causing end-to-end latency spikes and timeouts
description: Issue summary: Customers observed intermittent end-to-end request latency spikes and occasional 120s request timeouts for calls that use external tool invocation. Root cause traced to the new dynamic tool discovery / capability negotiation flow which performs a synchronous per-request capability check against the tool registry when a tool URL is present in the request. Impact: Multiple customers on Dedicated tier (BeaconHealth first reported) experienced increased p95/p99 latencies for requests that include tool invocation metadata. This caused some long-running customer calls to hit application-level timeouts and surface as 504/timeout errors. Environment: Prod (us-east-1), dedicated cluster for BeaconHealth. Regression window began ~2026-03-09 04:30 UTC, correlated with a router rollout that enabled dynamic negotiation by default.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer account on dedicated cluster with a request that includes a tool invocation (tool_url header + tool_schema omitted).
2) Send 50 concurrent generation requests with short prompt (~40 tokens) that trigger tool capability negotiation path.
3) Observe per-request traces and latency; p95 often spikes >800ms and tail >1.2s. Some requests hit client-side 60s/120s timeouts depending on caller config.
4) Toggle router feature flag 'dynamic_tool_negotiation' to false and repeat: p95 returns to baseline (~120-150ms).
observed_behavior: Service traces show synchronous RPC to tool-registry/service-discovery for capability negotiation on every request when a tool_url is present. Each negotiation adds 120-350ms depending on cache miss. Because negotiation is synchronous and blocking the request flow, overall request latency increases and tails spike. Customers reported 504/timeouts for long-running sessions and increased error rates on routes that combine short LLM generation with tool calls.
expected_behavior: Capability negotiation should be cached or executed asynchronously so that per-request overhead is minimized. On cache hit the latency overhead should be negligible (<10ms); on cache miss negotiation should use async prefetch or background warm-up without blocking the generation path.

investigation_notes: Initial triage: BeaconHealth reporting spikes 2026-03-09. Support ingested trace and found negotiation RPCs chained before generation start.
Distributed trace snippets show negotiation RPCs originate in router pre-handler and block the request path until capability resolution completes.
Perf profiling: cache hit latency ~8-12ms, cache miss latency 120-350ms due to remote schema fetch and TLS handshake to external tool endpoints.
Change correlation: router v2.14.0 rollout (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/112) enabled feature 'dynamic_tool_negotiation' by default on 2026-03-09 04:20 UTC.
Hypothesis: enabling negotiation by default exposed many requests with previously-unused tool_url header to synchronous negotiation path, dramatically increasing per-request hops and tail latency.
SRE confirmed increased 5xx/timeouts on dedicated clusters that had non-empty tool_url traffic patterns (coincides with BeaconHealth usage).
Customer provided sample request and agreed to run AB test toggling the flag; toggling off returned latencies to baseline within 5 minutes.
Related: SUP-99231 shows a similar symptom but was traced to preflight serialization—linked for follow-up harmonization of negotiation and preflight logic.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Asha Patel (Support): Customer BeaconHealth reported p99 spikes and intermittent 120s timeouts on routes containing tool_url. Added traces and sample requests to ticket.

2026-03-10 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Reproduced locally against a repro cluster; saw negotiation RPC per-request. Workaround: disable 'dynamic_tool_negotiation' feature flag on router—latency returns to baseline.

2026-03-11 - Elena Park (Customer Success): BeaconHealth confirmed that disabling the flag reduced errors and improved response times for their workloads. They're OK with a temporary workaround but request a permanent fix.

2026-03-11 - Ravi Shah (Engineers - Serving): We isolated the router change; PR 112 introduced negotiation middleware. Plan: add short-lived in-memory negotiation cache and background prewarm on first tool discovery. Will ship patch to router and serving-runtime.

2026-03-12 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Rolled out router patch v2.14.1 with negotiation cache (TTL=10m) to affected dedicated clusters at 2026-03-12 09:40 UTC. Monitoring shows p95/p99 back to normal and no new timeouts. Marking resolved pending customer confirmation.
2026-03-12 - BeaconHealth (Customer): Confirmed on 2026-03-12 12:05 UTC that error rate returned to baseline and no further timeouts observed.
resolution_notes: Workaround: For immediate relief customers can disable dynamic negotiation via router feature flag 'dynamic_tool_negotiation=false' or include tool_schema in request payload to avoid negotiation. Permanent fix: rolled out router v2.14.1 which adds an in-memory negotiation cache with TTL 10m and background prewarm on first tool discovery; also introduced a new header 'x-rw-tool-negotiation-mode' to opt into async-negotiation mode. Patch deployed 2026-03-12 09:40 UTC to affected dedicated clusters. Follow-ups: (1) extend cache to shared cache layer for multi-instance warm hits (INT-1124). (2) Add metrics for negotiation cache hit rate and per-request negotiation latency to Console dashboards (task created: ENG-ops backlog). Customer confirmed resolution on 2026-03-12.
